text.en: Why does your heart race when you are scared? Hormones, the chemical messengers of the body, take the message.

Hormones are chemical messengers made by endocrine glands and carried in blood to target organs.
Adrenaline from the adrenal gland prepares the body for fight or flight by raising heartbeat and blood to muscles.
Thyroxine from the thyroid regulates metabolism. It needs iodine; lack of iodine causes goitre.
Insulin from the pancreas lowers blood sugar. Lack of insulin causes diabetes.
Growth hormone from the pituitary controls growth; too little gives dwarfism and too much gives gigantism.
Testosterone in males and oestrogen in females control puberty changes.
Hormones act by feedback: when blood sugar rises, insulin is secreted, and when it falls, secretion is reduced.
Plant hormones: auxin (growth in the shoot tip), gibberellins (stem growth), cytokinins (cell division), abscisic acid (inhibits growth, wilting) and ethylene (fruit ripening).

problem.en: Why should we use iodised salt?

text.en: Iodine is required to make thyroxine.
Lack of iodine causes goitre, a swollen neck.

prompt.en: Name key hormones and their functions.
